title: Verified Measurement Credential: Audit-Grade AI Evidence — Council of AI Explained
context: 2026-09-01 engine cycle — answer-first page explaining the verified measurement credential as the audit trail primitive for AI governance; aligned to the Council of AI containment index and DEFONEOS-SEAL
body: A verified measurement credential is the cryptographic primitive that turns an AI measurement from a self-reported number into auditable evidence. When a model passes through a measurement axis on the Council of AI board, the result is not just a score — it is a signed record. The credential works like this: (1) the measurement run produces a structured output — which model, which axis, which items, what accuracy, what timestamp; (2) that output is hashed and signed with an Ed25519 key held by a recognised signing node — a node that is itself subject to governance rules about key custody and signing policy; (3) the signature is embedded in the record alongside the public key, so any party can verify offline that the record has not been altered since it was signed. This is not blockchain — there is no token, no distributed ledger, no consensus protocol. It is straightforward public-key signing, chosen because it is simple, fast, and already trusted by national cyber authorities. The credential is designed for three use cases. First, procurement gates: a buyer evaluating an AI tool can require that the vendor supply a verified measurement credential for the relevant axes, and verify it before signing the contract. Second, continuous monitoring: a deployed system can be re-measured on a schedule, and the sequence of signed credentials proves that drift was detected or ruled out. Third, regulatory filing: an operator submitting a conformity assessment under the EU AI Act, a FedRAMP OSCAL package, or a UK DRCF assurance return can attach verified measurement credentials as evidence rather than writing a narrative claim. The Council of AI does not certify — the credential says this was measured, here is the evidence, the evidence is intact. The certifier decides what it means.
